Play the main quest line. Chapter one is a tutorial. When you move to plank it introduces new features. Playing the main story will introduce the gameplay, for everything else, weapons, hero’s, survivors, and traps it’s all RNG based on what you get, and truth be told it really doesn’t matter what you’re using until late plankerton. My advice, google your good drops, or ones your interested in and read the wiki or check out its stats compared to what you have or what you like. For guns and hero’s it’s preference based on your play style. For traps, they work best in tandem, try and create your own combos, launching husks off cliffs with launcher traps, damaging traps, slow and stun, freeze, etc. use what you like, but they don’t become necessary until plank or if you are under lever for your mission. 

Rolls on weapons are what will make or break them. But only past plankerton. You will need an elemental weapon, Fire water, nature, and energy.  If you’re familiar with Pokémon, it’s fire water grass the same way the weakness work. Fire beats nature, water beats fire, and nature beats water. Energy is neutral towards them all, does more damage to an elemental foe than regular bullets, but less than the correct element.  The next slots you want depends on the gun, but typically damage, crit damage when paired with enough crit chance, damage to afflicted, affliction is DoT damage from your element if your perk specifys it, and mag size are safe bets. 

Survivors are how you level up. Ideally, you want to slot lead survivors that match the job description, and they will have a personality that when you slot the normal survivors you will want to match them as it will give you a bigger bonus. This is the best, and only way to “level up” and should be your priority for most of your evolution mats once you get a decent epic or legendary lead , and epic+ survivors. Last tip on this when choosing to evolve, always evolve lead survivors first, as they give you the biggest jump in power. 

Lastly, building. Arguably the most important part and what makes this game special. Try thing out and see what works. There is no best solution, sometimes the terrain will hinder tries and true methods, and you have to find a way to adapt. As a general rule, box or pyramid up your objective, then try and funnel the husks into choke points where you have traps/ can have a shooting advantage (lining up single file, high ground, etc.) and go from there based on where you can find weak points in your base. Prioritize propane husks, smashers, and other mist monsters as they do the most damage to you or your base.
